A hulking old rubber duck — cadmium yellow, mould seam riding up both flanks, its orange beak scuffed chalk-white at the tip from years of service — leads the squadron in a broad V, four smaller rubber ducklings strung out behind on each wing, their cobalt-blue eyes forward, the rearmost duckling riding backwards.

A dented hollow plastic shark, ox-blood red beneath and bone-white above, dorsal fin canted two degrees to port, runs in line abreast with a long low rubber crocodile — acid green, one eye patch worn to bare pale plastic — the two of them abreast, a body-length of open water between them where something has gone down.

A squat hollow plastic tugboat, burnt-orange hull and a bent black funnel, tows a rectangular kitchen sponge cut as a barge, riding so low only its yellow top-edge shows; three small round rubber ducks ride the barge as cargo, lashed together with a twist of ribbon, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted anchor.

A wind-up plastic frog — teal body, cadmium-yellow belly, wind-up key still turning at the stern — leads the group at a frantic churn, four hollow rubber ducks in a staggered echelon off its port side, each progressively smaller, the smallest barely a third the frog's length, a hairline crack sealed with a square of white plaster along its port side.

A grey rubber submarine, half-awash, water beading off its wet flanks and sheeting from its conning tower as it surfaces, pushes ahead of a loose V of five cadmium-yellow ducks, their wakes converging into a single broad turbulence astern, the submarine's mould seam showing clearly along the hull's full length, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted chevron.

A dozen small identical hollow plastic fish — each a flat vivid cobalt with a single painted red spot behind the gill — move as one tight school, tilting in unison to port, the body a perfect arrowhead aimed toward open water, three stragglers at the rear breaking formation and widening the shape.

A bristle scrubbing brush shipped upside down — its coarse white bristles as a hull, its ox-blood red spine riding high as a keel — lists five degrees to starboard; two small rubber ducks have been rafted one to each side with loops of elastic to keep it on course, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted chevron.

A long low rubber crocodile — deep viridian, bite-dents along the full length of its jaw, paint worn to bare pale plastic at the snout tip — leads a mixed fleet in a loose V: a hollow plastic penguin, a round rubber hippo, a flat rubber starfish, and a tiny moulded frogman figure clipped to the crocodile's back ridge as a pilot.

A rubber octopus — deep plum, two arms draped over the hull of a dented hollow plastic tugboat beneath it, six arms trailing in the water — rides at the tug’s bow with both arms forward, four small ducks in a staggered line off the tug’s port side, the rearmost duck tethered by a short length of twine to the duck ahead of it, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted eye.

A plastic pirate boat — acid green, its mast chewed ragged at the tip and canted hard to starboard — leads a V of three hollow rubber ducks, each duck a different saturated colour: ox-blood, cobalt, burnt orange; the formation tight except for one straggler hull-down at the rear, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted star.

A wind-up hollow plastic penguin — chalk-white breast, jet-black back, orange flippers churning — thrashes at the rear of a loose group of six cadmium-yellow rubber ducks spread wide across the water ahead of it, the penguin closing the gap at every stroke, its wind-up key clicking audibly at each rotation.

A soap-dish raft — bone-white, heavy with absorbed water, riding two centimetres of freeboard — has a facecloth rigged as a sail, the cloth deep cobalt, sagging and stretched with weight; two small round rubber ducks stand on the foredeck as lookouts, and a third has been lashed to the mast halfway up, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted curl of gilt.

A net bath scrubby — tangled mesh, burnt orange, wallowing with water pooled in every hollow — moves as a troop transport, nine small identical rubber ducks packed into its mesh, only their cadmium-yellow heads showing above the weave, the whole mass pushed from behind by a single wind-up frog whose key still turns at the stern.

An enormous old cadmium-yellow rubber duck — squeaker hole visible at its base, mould seam running ear to tail, a patch of bare pale rubber where the paint has gone on its left cheek — moves in line abreast with a second duck of equal size, a half-body-length of open water between them, the gap held exactly.

Five rubber ducks in line abreast — every one of them cadmium yellow, every one of them identical — except the fourth: a pale-blue impostor of the same mould and the same size, riding in perfect station, the same scuffed beak, the same squeaker hole, indistinguishable except by colour from the ducks ahead and behind.

A mixed-medium fleet in a loose V, every vessel a different animal: a teal hollow plastic whale leads, then a burnt-orange rubber starfish, then a cobalt hollow plastic dolphin, then a deep-plum rubber octopus one arm trailing, then a chalk-white hollow plastic seal, then a tiny acid-green rubber turtle bringing up the rear, each a genuinely different silhouette.

A hollow plastic beaker — ox-blood red, inverted, slowly going down bow-first as a bathysphere — trails a rope of twine back to a flat rubber raft where three cadmium-yellow ducks watch the descent in tight formation, the beaker's base still just above the surface, water climbing its sides as it descends, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted star.

Eleven rubber ducks rafted tight into a floating island — cadmium yellow, cobalt, and burnt orange packed so close their hulls touch — the whole mass moving as one body, rotating slowly clockwise, a single very large rubber duck riding at the centre elevated half a centimetre above the rest on account of the crowd beneath it.

A dented hollow plastic tugboat — deep cobalt hull, chalk-white superstructure, one porthole cracked and re-sealed with a square of white plaster — leads a loose line of five rubber animals spread across the water to either side of it: a yellow duck, a green crocodile, a red crab, a plum octopus, a burnt-orange starfish, each holding its own station, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted stripe.

A rubber duck — the largest, oldest, most sun-faded in the fleet, its yellow now nearly white at the crown, its orange beak cracked along the lower jaw — rides at the head of a V of fourteen ducklings, each duckling barely a quarter the leader’s length, the V so long the rearmost pair are hull-down at the edge of the frame.

A long low rubber crocodile — acid green, its mould seam raised along the full spine, bite-dents bracketing the snout — carries a rubber octopus amidships, two plum arms hooked over the crocodile's back ridge; three small hollow plastic fish — cobalt, ox-blood, and burnt orange — hold position in a tight triangle off the starboard bow.

A hollow plastic submarine — battleship grey, water still sheeting off the conning tower mid-surface, a dent pressed into the port side of the hull — pushes up into a loose line of six cadmium-yellow rubber ducks from below and astern, the ducks fanning wide to both sides as the grey hull rises between them, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted anchor.

A hollow plastic whale — chalk-white, blue-grey along the dorsal ridge, a hairline crack sealed with clear tape that has begun to peel at one end — leads a loose V of five rubber sea creatures in a slow arc to starboard: a teal dolphin, a plum jellyfish, a burnt-orange crab, an acid-green turtle, a cadmium-yellow rubber duck that has joined the wrong fleet.

Two hollow plastic tugboats in line abreast — one ox-blood with a chalk-white funnel, one cobalt with a burnt-orange funnel — each tow a sponge barge half their own length, the barges riding so low their cargoes of small rubber ducks are nearly at water level; a fifth duck has jumped between the two barges and sits in open water between the two tows, its flanks and panels each one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted chevron.

A scuffed rubber duck — cadmium yellow, squeaker hole gaping at the base, mould seam showing on both flanks — rides at the point of a V of eight ducks in two precise diagonal lines; the last duck on the starboard wing has a smaller duck rafted flush to its port side by a loop of green ribbon, the two of them moving as one hull, a crew of one carrying a passenger.
